title: How to build a CRDT from scratch
author: Julia Evans
snippet: Step-by-step implementation of a CRDT for a collaborative text editor. We build a simple G-Counter, then a PN-Counter, and finally a full LWW-Register in Rust with tests.

title: Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types
author: Shapiro et al.
snippet: Original CRDT paper defining the mathematical framework for convergent and commutative replicated data types. Proves eventual consistency without coordination.

title: My experience building CRDTs in production
author: Alex Chen
snippet: What actually went wrong when we deployed CRDTs at scale, including memory blowup from tombstones, clock skew issues, and how we fixed them.

title: automerge/automerge
author: Martin Kleppmann
snippet: A JSON-like data structure that can be modified concurrently by different users, and merged again automatically. Implements CRDTs for rich text, lists, and maps.

title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
author: Fielding et al.
snippet: Defines the semantics of HTTP: request methods, status codes, header and trailer fields, and content negotiation. Supersedes RFC 7231.

title: In defense of simple architectures
author: Dan Luu
snippet: Wave is a $1.7B company with 70M users that runs a monolith on Postgres. Sometimes the boring choice is the right choice. Data on when microservices help and when they don't.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report
author: OpenAI
snippet: Technical report on GPT-4, a large-scale multimodal model. Reports performance on academic benchmarks, professional exams, and discusses safety mitigations.

title: BurntSushi/ripgrep
author: Andrew Gallant
snippet: A line-oriented search tool that recursively searches directories for a regex pattern. Combines the usability of The Silver Searcher with the speed of grep.

title: How to remove all git branches which have been merged
author: Adam Dymitruk
snippet: git branch --merged | egrep -v '(^\*|master|main|dev)' | xargs git branch -d. This safely removes only branches that have been fully merged into the current branch.

title: When your filesystem lies to you about fsync
author: Rachel Kroll
snippet: Discovery that certain filesystem and drive combinations silently ignore fsync, leading to data loss on power failure. Includes test methodology and affected hardware.

title: Attention Is All You Need
author: Vaswani et al.
snippet: Introduces the Transformer architecture, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Achieves state-of-the-art on machine translation with parallelizable training.

title: The Absolute Minimum Every Developer Must Know About Unicode
author: Nikita Tonsky
snippet: No excuses in 2023. Covers UTF-8, code points vs grapheme clusters, normalization forms, and why string length is a meaningless concept. With visual examples.

title: meilisearch/meilisearch
author: Meilisearch
snippet: A lightning-fast search engine that fits effortlessly into your apps. Written in Rust. Typo-tolerant, faceted, sortable. Instant search with <50ms response times.

title: I don't think Zig is the right language for me
author: Drew DeVault
snippet: After years of advocacy, a critical look at where Zig falls short: compile times, debugging experience, and the allocator-everywhere pattern. Comparison with Rust and C.

title: Machine Learning for Electronic Health Records
author: Rajkomar et al.
snippet: Survey of ML techniques applied to EHR data. Covers patient outcome prediction, clinical NLP, and privacy-preserving federated learning approaches.

title: Why SQLite is the only database you need for most apps
author: Ben Johnson
snippet: Litestream + SQLite gives you streaming replication, point-in-time recovery, and zero operational overhead. Benchmarks showing it handles 50K reads/sec easily.

title: How LLMs work, from scratch
author: Eli Bendersky
snippet: Ground-up explanation of transformer language models. Tokenization, embeddings, attention mechanism, and generation — all with minimal code examples in Python.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs
author: Yao et al.
snippet: Framework for LLM reasoning that explores multiple reasoning paths, evaluates states, and uses search algorithms (BFS/DFS) to navigate the solution space.

title: astral-sh/ruff
author: Charlie Marsh
snippet: An extremely fast Python linter and formatter, written in Rust. 10-100x faster than existing tools. Drop-in replacement for Flake8, isort, and Black.

title: Using Nix Flakes in production for two years
author: Xe Iaso
snippet: Honest retrospective on Nix Flakes: what works (reproducible builds, dev environments), what doesn't (documentation, error messages, learning curve). With practical patterns.
